mainTopic: Windpipe damage measures, the valid area of the neck for שחיטה, and the brain membranes
overview: This amud opens with the last line of a story, where a sage says that people who honor him are really honoring themselves. Then the גמרא turns to damage in the windpipe (קנה). Holes that remove real material add up toward the size of an איסר coin. Tiny sieve-like holes that remove almost nothing add up toward a majority of the windpipe's circumference, like a cut. For a bird, whose windpipe is too small for an איסר, the damaged piece is folded over the opening, and if it covers most of it the bird is טרפה. The גמרא also rules on a door-like flap and on a crack along the length. On the crack, רבי יוחנן says any tiny whole bit at the top and bottom is enough. Next it marks the area of the neck valid for שחיטה, which is the stretch the animal extends naturally while grazing, and it defines the חזה. Finally it discusses a hole in the brain's membranes and where the brain ends and the חוט השדרה begins. That last answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the story: honoring me is their honor
steps.stepSummary: The sage finishes the earlier story by explaining that when people honor him, the honor is really theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is an honor for them that they honor me.
steps.whatsHappening: This line closes a story from the previous section. The sage explains why he lets people honor him: it is good for them, not for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sage does not see the respect people show him as something he gains. He sees it as a chance for them to gain merit by honoring Torah. With this line the story ends, and the גמרא is ready to start a new halachic topic.

keyTerms.meaning: an honor for them; they are honored

phrases.english: It is an honor for them that they honor me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story from the previous section of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Honoring a Torah scholar benefits the people who give the honor.

steps.title: Many tiny holes in the windpipe add up to a majority
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: if the windpipe has many tiny holes like a sieve, the holes join together toward a 'majority' of the windpipe's circumference.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: If the windpipe was pierced with holes like a sieve, the holes join together to make up a majority.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב rules that many tiny holes in the windpipe are added together, and they are measured against 'most of the way around' the windpipe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A windpipe cut through most of its circumference makes the animal a טריפה. רב says that tiny sieve-like holes count toward that 'majority' measurement. He does not measure them against the איסר size that is used for a hole in the windpipe. This choice is exactly what the next step will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: it was pierced; it got holes
they join together; they are added up
a majority; here, most of the windpipe's circumference

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse two different measurements. 'Majority' (רובא) means most of the way around the windpipe, which counts like a cut. 'איסר' is the size of a small coin, which counts like a hole. רב is telling us which of the two the tiny holes are measured against.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
If it was pierced like a sieve,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the windpipe (קנה). A נפה is a sieve, so picture lots of tiny holes.

phrases.english: they join together to make up a majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new halachic topic after the story ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tiny sieve-like holes in the windpipe are added together and measured against a majority of its circumference.

steps.title: Challenge from the holes in a skull
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה argues from a ברייתא about a skull: small holes join together toward that case's own measurement. So holes in the windpipe should join together toward an איסר, not toward a majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה objected: A skull that has one long hole, or even many holes, the holes join together to make up the size of a drill hole. This shows that since the skull's measurement is a drill hole, the holes join toward a drill hole. So here too, since the windpipe's measurement is an איסר, the holes should join toward an איסר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ירמיה challenges רב's ruling. He brings a case where small holes are measured against the normal measurement for that case, and says the windpipe should work the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the skull case, small holes are added together toward the skull's usual hole measurement, the size of a drill hole. The windpipe's usual hole measurement is an איסר. So by comparison, the tiny holes should be added toward an איסר, and רב's 'majority' looks like the wrong measurement.

keyTerms.meaning: the size of a drill hole, a fixed measurement
the set measurement for a law
the size of an איסר, a small coin

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: וּבְגוּלְגּוֹלֶת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ נֶקֶב אֶחָד אָרוֹךְ,
phrases.english: And a skull that has one long hole,
even if it has many holes,
they join together to make up the size of a drill hole.
This shows that since its measurement is the size of a drill hole,
they join together toward the size of a drill hole.
Here too, since its measurement is the size of an issar,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the windpipe. A hole the size of an איסר in the windpipe makes the animal a טריפה.

phrases.english: they should join together toward the size of an issar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that tiny holes in the windpipe are measured against a majority of the circumference.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא about the skull shows that small holes add up toward that case's own hole measurement. So holes in the windpipe should add up toward its own hole measurement, an איסר.

steps.title: Holes that remove material versus tiny holes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב ירמיה missed another teaching of רב. Holes that remove real material join toward an איסר. Tiny holes that remove almost nothing join toward a majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: He forgot what רבי חלבו said in the name of רב חמא בר גוריא, who said in the name of רב: Holes that remove some material join together toward an איסר. Holes that do not remove material join together toward a majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב ירמיה's challenge. It says he missed a teaching of רב that explains when holes are measured against an איסר and when against a majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some holes actually remove a piece of the windpipe. Those holes are added together toward an איסר, the same way the skull's holes are added toward a drill hole. Tiny sieve-like holes remove almost nothing, so the windpipe is not missing a piece. Instead they weaken it the way a cut does, so they are measured against a majority, like a cut.

keyTerms.meaning: it slipped his mind; he missed it

steps.whatToRemember: The kind of hole decides how it is measured. Holes that remove material add up toward an איסר, just like a hole. Tiny holes that remove nothing add up toward a majority of the circumference, just like a cut.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains רב's first ruling. The 'majority' measurement in step 2 was about sieve-like holes, which remove nothing, so it does not contradict the skull case.

phrases.english: It slipped his mind, this that Rabbi Ḥelbo said,
phrases.notes: 'His mind' means רב ירמיה, the one who asked the question.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
Holes that remove some material
join together toward the size of an issar,
and those that do not remove material,
join together toward a majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ירמיה's challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between two types of holes, using another teaching of רב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All holes in the windpipe should be added together toward an איסר, the same way the skull's holes are added toward a drill hole.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only holes that remove material are added toward an איסר. Tiny sieve-like holes, which remove nothing, are added toward a majority, like a cut.

steps.title: A removed strip joins toward an איסר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that when a strip is taken out of the windpipe, its area counts toward the measure of an איסר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: If a strip was removed from the windpipe, it joins together toward the size of an איסר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching is given about a different kind of damage: a long, thin strip cut out of the windpipe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A strip may be too narrow to fit an איסר coin anywhere along it. Even so, we add up its whole area, and if the total equals an איסר, it counts. This is real missing material, so it fits the איסר side of the rule from Step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: A strip; a long, thin piece
It joins together; it adds up
A small coin, used here as a measure of size

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
If a strip was removed from it,
it joins together toward an issar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another case where missing material is measured by an איסר, in line with the distinction in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A strip removed from the windpipe adds up toward the size of an איסר.

steps.title: What if the windpipe is pierced like a sieve?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר נחמני asks רבי יהושע בן לוי about a windpipe full of tiny holes, like a sieve.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר נחמני asked רבי יהושע בן לוי: If the windpipe was pierced like a sieve, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A student asks his teacher a clear question about a windpipe with many small holes. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is how to measure many separate small holes. Do they add up toward an איסר, toward a majority, or not at all?

keyTerms.meaning: Like a sieve (from נָפָה, a sieve)
What is it? What is the law?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani asked
of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
If it was pierced like a sieve, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the same sieve-like case that רב ruled on in Step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the many small holes of a sieve-like windpipe are measured.

steps.title: Holes that remove material versus holes that do not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers: holes that remove material join toward an איסר, and holes that remove almost nothing join toward a majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The חכמים said: Holes that take away material join together toward an איסר. Holes that do not take away material join together toward a majority.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers the question by quoting an established rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same distinction the גמרא used in Step 4 to answer רב ירמיה. Now we see it was a known rule ("הרי אמרו") and not only a teaching of רב. The kind of hole decides the measure: real missing material is measured by an איסר, and tiny holes that remove almost nothing are measured by a majority.

keyTerms.meaning: They have already said; this is an established rule
A loss of material; something actually missing
A majority (here, most of the windpipe)

steps.whatToRemember: Holes with real missing material add up to an איסר. Holes with almost nothing missing add up to a majority.

phrases.english: He said to him: They have said:
Holes that have a loss of material
join together toward an issar,
and those that have no loss of material
join together toward a majority.
phrases.notes: A majority of the windpipe, just like רב said back in Step 2.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 6 and confirms the distinction from Step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Holes with missing material are measured by an איסר. Holes without missing material are measured by a majority.

steps.title: What is the measure for a bird?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how missing material is measured in a bird's windpipe.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a bird, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question that the next step will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird's windpipe is very small, so an איסר measure for missing material does not work well. The גמרא needs a different way to measure for birds.

phrases.english: With a bird, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the איסר measure from Step 7 to birds and asks how it would work there.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The size of missing material that makes a bird's windpipe טרפה.

steps.title: Fold the damaged piece over the windpipe's opening
steps.stepSummary: Quoting רבי אלעזר, רבי יצחק בר נחמני teaches: fold the damaged piece and lay it on the opening of the windpipe. If it covers most of the opening, the bird is טרפה. רב פפא gives the memory aid of a sieve.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר נחמני said: רבי אלעזר explained this to me personally. One folds it and lays it on the opening of the windpipe. If it covers most of the windpipe, it is טרפה. If not, it is כשרה. רב פפא said: Your memory aid is a sieve.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the bird question with a hands-on test, and רב פפא adds a way to remember it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a bird, an איסר is not used as the measure. Instead the damaged piece is compared to the bird's own windpipe. If it covers most of the opening, it is a majority, and the bird is טרפה. The sieve memory aid connects to the sieve-like holes in Step 6: picture laying the piece over the opening like a sieve.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani said:
It was explained to me personally
by Rabbi Elazar:
One folds it and lays it on the opening of the windpipe,
phrases.notes: "It" is the damaged piece of the windpipe.

phrases.aramaic: אִם חוֹפֶה אֶת רוֹב הַקָּנֶה – טְרֵפָה,
phrases.english: if it covers most of the windpipe, it is a tereifa,
and if not, it is kosher.
Rav Pappa said:
And your memory aid is a sieve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the bird question from Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For a bird, fold the damaged piece over the opening. If it covers most of the opening, the bird is טרפה. If not, it is כשרה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a measure can change to fit the size of the animal. For birds, the bird's own windpipe is the measure.

steps.title: A piece hanging like a door
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that a door-shaped flap in the windpipe makes the animal טרפה if the opening is big enough for an איסר to fit across its width.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the windpipe was broken open like a door, רב נחמן said: the measure is when an איסר can enter it across its width.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new kind of damage: a flap cut on several sides that still hangs on by one side, like a door on a hinge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is how big this flap-shaped opening must be. רב נחמן says the opening must be large enough for an איסר coin to fit inside it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was broken open; it has a gap

phrases.english: If it was broken open like a door,
phrases.notes: Picture a flap that is cut free on most sides but still attached on one side, like a door on a hinge.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
enough that an issar can enter across its width.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from holes to another kind of windpipe damage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A door-shaped gap makes the animal טרפה when an איסר can fit across its width.

steps.title: A lengthwise crack stays kosher if the end rings remain
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a windpipe cracked along its length is כשרה, even if only one whole ring is left at the top and one at the bottom.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the windpipe was cracked, רב said: Even if only one ring was left whole at the top and one ring at the bottom, it is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב's ruling on a long crack running along the windpipe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A crack along the length does not take away material. As long as one complete ring holds the windpipe together above the crack and another holds it below, the animal stays כשרה, even if the rest is split.

keyTerms.meaning: It was cracked or split (along its length)
A ring or segment of the windpipe

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with holes or missing pieces. A crack along the length takes nothing away, so the measure here is whether whole rings are left at both ends, not an איסר or a majority.

phrases.english: If it was cracked, Rav said:
Even if nothing was left in it except
one ring above
and one ring below,
it is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of windpipe damage types with a lengthwise crack.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lengthwise crack is כשרה as long as one whole ring remains above it and one below it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: rings do not matter, any tiny bit is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rejects the 'one ring' detail in רב's ruling. Even if only a tiny bit of whole windpipe remains above and below the crack, the animal is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told רב's ruling to רבי יוחנן. He said: Why does רב talk about a 'ring'? Rather, say: even if only a tiny bit stayed whole above and a tiny bit below, the animal is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן hears רב's ruling from Step 11 and rejects the requirement of a whole ring at each end. He restates the rule: any tiny whole amount at the top and bottom is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב required one full ring at the top and one at the bottom. רבי יוחנן says the ring is not the point. All that matters is that the crack does not run the entire length, so even a tiny whole piece at each end keeps the animal כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say it this way (a restating of a ruling)
A tiny amount, any amount at all

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not making things stricter. He is being more lenient than the 'one ring' wording: even less than a ring is enough.

phrases.english: They said it before Rabbi Yochanan,
phrases.notes: 'It' means רב's ruling from the last step, about the windpipe cracked along its length.

phrases.english: He said: What is this 'ring' and what is that 'ring'
phrases.notes: He means: why bring rings into it at all?

phrases.english: that Rav says?
Rather, say:
Even if nothing remained in it
except a tiny bit above
and a tiny bit below, it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה חוּלְיָא וּמָה חוּלְיָא דְּקָאָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects and restates the 'one ring' detail of רב's ruling in Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the 'whole ring' requirement, not רב's basic ruling that a crack along the length is כשרה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ring size is irrelevant. What matters is that some whole tissue remains at each end.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A windpipe cracked along its length is כשרה as long as any tiny amount stays whole above and below.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is pleased that רבי יונתן agrees
steps.stepSummary: The same explanation was reported to רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי יונתן, and he happily says the Babylonian scholars understood it the way he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told רבי יוחנן this same explanation in the name of רבי יונתן. He said to them: Do our Babylonian friends know how to explain it with this reasoning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that רבי יונתן explained רב's ruling the same way as רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן is glad to hear the Babylonians agree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds support to רבי יוחנן's reading from Step 12. A second scholar on his own reached the same explanation, 'any tiny bit is enough,' so this reading of רב is strengthened.

keyTerms.meaning: Our Babylonian friends (the scholars of בבל)

phrases.english: They said it before Rabbi Yochanan
in the name of Rabbi Yonatan, like this,
phrases.notes: 'Like this' means the same explanation רבי יוחנן just gave: any tiny bit above and below is enough.

phrases.english: He said to them: Do our Babylonian friends know
how to explain according to this reasoning?
phrases.notes: This is said with happy surprise, not as a complaint. He is glad they agree.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָדְעִין חַבְרִין בַּבְלָאֵי לְפָרוֹשֵׁי כִּי הַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms רבי יוחנן's explanation from Step 12 with a matching explanation from רבי יונתן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's reading that any tiny whole amount above and below is enough.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יונתן's matching explanation, reported to רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatToRemember: A windpipe cracked along its length is כשרה if even a tiny whole bit remains at the top and bottom. Both רבי יוחנן and רבי יונתן read רב this way.

steps.title: The whole neck is fit for slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר יוסף teaches a ברייתא: שחיטה is valid along the whole neck, from the top ring of the windpipe down to the 'lower' edges of the lung.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר יוסף taught before רבי יוחנן: The entire neck is fit for שחיטה, from the large ring down to the lower edges of the lung.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: where along the neck a valid שחיטה can be done. A ברייתא gives the top and bottom limits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The top limit is the large uppermost ring of the windpipe. The bottom limit is called the 'lower edges of the lung,' which seems odd. רבא will explain that wording in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The large ring, the uppermost ring of the windpipe

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵא רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Yosef taught before Rabbi Yochanan:
The whole neck, all of it,
is fit for slaughter,
from the large ring
phrases.notes: This is the big top ring of the windpipe, near the head.

phrases.english: until the lower edges of the lung.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵא רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the valid area of the neck for שחיטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שחיטה is valid along the whole neck, from the top ring down to the edges of the lung.

steps.title: רבא explains 'lower' and limits the area to the natural grazing stretch
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the 'lower' edges of the lung really means the upper edges. The valid area is the part of the neck the animal stretches out on its own while grazing, as long as it is not forced.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: 'Lower' means the edge that is really the upper one. For I say: all the area the animal stretches its neck out to while grazing is valid, as long as it is not forced.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the confusing word 'lower' in the ברייתא and gives a clear rule for the bottom limit of the neck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal hangs upside down, the edge of the lung nearest the head looks like the 'lower' one. So the ברייתא really means the top of the lung. רבא defines the valid zone as the length of neck the animal naturally extends when grazing, not extra length gained by stretching it by force.

keyTerms.meaning: Stretches its neck out and grazes
As long as it is not forced

steps.confusionAlert: 'Lower' here does not mean the bottom of the lung. רבא says it means the edge closest to the head, as seen when the animal hangs upside down.

phrases.english: Rava said: 'lower' means the one that is upper,
phrases.notes: Picture the animal hanging by its feet: the top of the lung now looks like the bottom.

phrases.english: for I say
all the area to which it stretches its neck and grazes,
provided that it is not forced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the confusing wording of the ברייתא in Step 14 and defines its limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The valid area for שחיטה is the length of neck the animal naturally stretches when grazing, without being forced.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical bottom limit for where a שוחט may cut, and it raises the question in the next step about an animal that stretches itself.

steps.title: What if the animal stretched itself? Left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא (or רב חנניה) asks about an animal that stretched its own neck further than usual. Is the extra area valid? The question stays unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא, and some say רב חנניה, asked: If the animal forced itself, what is the law? Let it stand (תיקו).
steps.whatsHappening: A question is asked about רבא's rule: what if no person forced the animal, but it stretched itself extra far? The גמרא has no answer and leaves it as תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the area counts only if the animal is not forced. The doubt is whether stretching by its own choice counts like natural grazing or like being forced. The question is left open.

keyTerms.meaning: It forced itself, stretched itself beyond normal
Let it stand, the question remains unresolved

phrases.english: Rav Chanina asked,
and some say Rav Chananya:
If it forced itself, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means the animal stretched its neck extra far by itself. Does that extra area count as valid?

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב חֲנִינָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב חֲנַנְיָה: אָנְסָה עַצְמָהּ מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the edge of רבא's 'not forced' condition from Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the extra neck area is valid when the animal stretched itself rather than being forced by a person.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No answer. The question remains תיקו.

steps.title: Forcing the neck and slaughtering makes the שחיטה invalid
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש rule that if the שוחט forced the סימנים to stretch and then cut in the extra area, the שחיטה is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי שמעון בן לקיש sat together, and a ruling came out from them: If he forced the סימנים and slaughtered, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a clear ruling from רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש: a person stretching the neck by force and cutting low makes the שחיטה invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches רבא's condition 'as long as it is not forced.' Unlike the open question about an animal stretching itself, here a person did the forcing, so the extra area does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: A ruling came out from between them (they agreed on it together)
He forced the סימנים, stretched the neck by force
The windpipe and food pipe, which are cut in שחיטה

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish sat,
a matter came out from between them:
If he forced the simanim and slaughtered, it is invalid.
phrases.notes: He means he stretched the neck by force and cut in the low part that is only reached by stretching.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ, נְפַק מִילְּתָא מִבֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a firm ruling for the case where a person forces the stretch, in line with רבא's condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the שוחט forces the neck to stretch and cuts in the extra area, the שחיטה is invalid.
steps.whatToRemember: Valid שחיטה is only in the neck area the animal naturally extends while grazing. Forcing the stretch and cutting there is פסולה, while an animal stretching itself is left as תיקו.

steps.title: A hole in the windpipe below the chest is judged like the lung
steps.stepSummary: A second ruling from רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש: a hole in the windpipe below the chest is treated like a hole in the lung.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the windpipe was pierced below the chest, it is judged like the lung.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another ruling from the same discussion: the low part of the windpipe, below the chest, follows the rules of the lung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole in the upper windpipe needs a certain size, such as an איסר from Step 7, to make the animal טרפה. Below the chest, the windpipe is treated like the lung, where any hole at all makes the animal טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The windpipe was pierced (has a hole)
Is judged like the lung, follows the lung's rules

phrases.english: If the windpipe was perforated below the chest,
it is judged like the lung.
phrases.notes: For the lung, any hole at all makes it טרפה, so no minimum size is needed here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling from the same discussion of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, about the lowest part of the windpipe.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hole in the windpipe below the chest is judged like a hole in the lung.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the size rules for windpipe holes from earlier steps apply only to the upper windpipe.

steps.title: What exactly is the breast
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines the חזה given to the כהנים. It is the part facing the ground, from the neck to the כרס, including two ribs from each side.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Which part is the breast? It is the part that faces the ground. Going one way it reaches the neck, and going the other way it reaches the rumen. You cut two ribs from each side, and this is the breast given to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that defines the חזה. Step 18 spoke about a hole in the windpipe 'below the חזה,' so we need to know where the חזה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חזה is the underside of the animal, the part that faces the ground. It is not the ribbed sides. Its length runs from the neck to the כרס, and it includes two ribs cut from each side. That defined piece is the one given to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: The breast or chest of the animal

phrases.english: The Sages taught: Which is the breast?
This is the part that faces the ground,
below, until the neck,
phrases.notes: Picture the animal hanging by its legs, so 'below' points toward the head.

phrases.english: above, until the rumen.
He cuts two ribs from the two sides
on this side and that side,
and this is the breast that is given to the priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines 'חזה,' the boundary used in step 18's ruling about a hole in the windpipe.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חזה is the underside from the neck to the כרס, including two ribs from each side. This is the piece given to the כהנים.

steps.title: A pierced outer brain membrane is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a pierced brain membrane. רב and שמואל rule that piercing the outer membrane alone makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if the membrane of the brain was pierced. רב and שמואל both say: this means the upper membrane, even if the lower one was not pierced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new case in the משנה, a hole in the brain's membrane. רב and שמואל explain which membrane the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brain has two membranes, an outer one near the skull and an inner one touching the brain. According to this version of רב and שמואל, a hole in the outer one alone already makes the animal a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Upper, here meaning the outer membrane
Lower, here meaning the inner membrane
An animal with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten

phrases.english: If the membrane of the brain was pierced.
Rav and Shmuel, who both say:
The upper membrane,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אִינְּקִיב תַּתָּאָה.
phrases.english: even though the lower one was not pierced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה: the brain membrane.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hole in the outer brain membrane alone makes the animal a טרפה.

steps.title: Second version: the inner membrane must be pierced
steps.stepSummary: A different version of רב and שמואל's ruling says the animal is not a טרפה unless the inner membrane is pierced too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: it is only a טרפה once the lower membrane is pierced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of what רב and שמואל said. This version needs more damage before the animal becomes a טרפה, so it is more lenient: a hole in the outer membrane alone is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, a hole in the outer membrane alone does not make the animal a טרפה. Only a hole that reaches the inner membrane does.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new rabbi arguing. It is the same רב and שמואל, reported in a second way.

phrases.english: And some say: not until the lower one is pierced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative version of step 20's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a hole in the inner membrane makes the animal a טרפה.

steps.title: A memory sign pointing to the inner membrane
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני gives a sign to remember the rule: the 'bag the brain rests in,' which is the inner membrane.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: and your sign is the bag in which the brain rests.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר נחמני gives a memory trick so we remember which membrane counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'bag the brain rests in' is the inner membrane, which holds the brain directly. The sign points to the inner membrane as the one that matters, which fits the second version in step 21.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two brain membranes. One version says the outer one is enough to make a טרפה. The other, backed by the memory sign, requires a hole in the inner one.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said:
And your sign is:
the bag in which the brain rests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a memory sign that matches the version requiring the inner membrane.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The membrane that counts is the bag holding the brain, the inner one.

steps.title: The thin membrane is easy to see in the testicles
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי notes that a membrane matching the brain's inner one is easy to see in the testicles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: its counterpart is noticeable in the testicles.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a way to picture the thin inner membrane. A similar membrane can be clearly seen around the testicles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inner brain membrane is very thin and hard to notice. Pointing to a similar, visible membrane in the testicles helps us know what this layer looks like.

keyTerms.meaning: Its counterpart, the thing that matches it

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Its counterpart in the testicles is noticeable.
phrases.notes: 'Its counterpart' means a thin membrane like the brain's inner one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Helps us picture the inner membrane named in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A membrane like the inner brain membrane can be clearly seen in the testicles.

steps.title: Where the brain ends and the spinal cord begins
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא teaches that everything inside the skull counts as מוח. Once it starts to stretch out, it counts as חוט השדרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן פזי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, quoting בר קפרא: Brain means everything inside the skull, and all of it is treated as brain. Once it starts to stretch out, it is treated as the spinal cord.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching draws the line between the brain and the spinal cord. The two have different טרפה rules, so the line matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whatever sits inside the skull is judged by the rules of the brain. The part that begins to extend like a cord is judged by the rules of the חוט השדרה. This sets up the next question: where exactly does the stretching start?

keyTerms.meaning: Is judged as, follows the rules of

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in the name of bar Kappara:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹחַ – כׇּל מַה שֶּׁבַּקְּדֵירָה נִדּוֹן כְּמוֹחַ,
phrases.english: Brain: everything that is in the skull is judged as brain;
phrases.notes: The skull is called a 'pot' here because it holds the brain.

phrases.english: once it begins to stretch out, it is judged as the spinal cord.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוֹחַ – כׇּל מַה שֶּׁבַּקְּדֵירָה נִדּוֹן כְּמוֹחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the membranes to the boundary between brain and spinal cord.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everything inside the skull counts as brain, and the part that stretches out counts as spinal cord.

steps.title: Where does the stretching begin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks at what exact point the brain begins to stretch out into the spinal cord.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where does it begin to stretch out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact starting point of the חוט השדרה. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 gave a general rule but no exact place. To use the rule in practice, we need a clear marker for where the brain ends.

phrases.english: And from where does it begin to stretch out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact boundary behind step 24's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact physical point where the brain becomes the spinal cord.

steps.title: An answer heard directly from רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר נחמני begins to answer with an explanation he heard directly from רבי יהושע בן לוי, describing a marker 'like two' things.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר נחמני said: It was explained to me personally by רבי יהושע בן לוי: something like two...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק בר נחמני starts to answer the question, using what he heard firsthand from רבי יהושע בן לוי. His description is cut off here and continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He stresses that he heard this directly, which makes the report reliable. The answer will describe a physical marker shaped 'like two' things, and the rest of the description comes next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Naḥmani said:
To me it was explained personally
by Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi himself:
something like two

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִידִי מִיפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 25's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A firsthand report from רבי יהושע בן לוי describing a marker 'like two' things. The full description continues in the next part of the גמרא.
